newsitem.title: USA: Hearst property caught up in fraud case.
newsitem.headline: Hearst property caught up in fraud case.

text.p: Officials Monday accused the former head of a New York City-funded agency of stealing almost $3 million -- money he spent to buy property from a member of the wealthy Hearst family who refuses to return it.

Michael Pope, who ran the Richard Allen Center on Life foster-care agency, gave Veronica Hearst $2.3 million for her 45-acre estate in Armonk, New York, said Manhattan District Attorney Robert Morgenthau.
Hearst is the wife of Randolph Hearst, former chairman of the Hearst Corp., and stepmother to heiress Patty Hearst.
"Hearst has declined to return the money," the district attorney said, adding that there was no evidence to indicate that she knew the money was stolen.
Authorities may have to sue Hearst to get the money back, he said. An attorney for Hearst did not return telephone calls seeking comment.
The Hearst estate includes a quarry, and Pope wanted to use the property to bottle water, the prosecutor said. The estate is about 25 miles north of New York City.
Pope is charged with grand larceny and bribery and, if convicted, faces up to 25 years in prison.

He was elected to head the foster-care agency in mid-November 1995 and two weeks later began making unauthorized transfers from its bank account into one of his own at Merrill Lynch, authorities said. He also applied for a line of credit using the agency's name, they said.
The alleged theft was uncovered in March 1996 when the Administration for Children's Services, which monitors RACOL, discovered a $2.8 million overpayment and demanded its money back.
Richard Ross, a former Merrill Lynch stockbroker also charged in connection with the thefts, pleaded guilty last week to criminal possession of stolen property. He faces up to seven years in prison.
